rationale: EXPERIMENTAL ANCHOR. Ca affinity measured: ~5x lower in isolated cbEGF32, ~9x in the TB6-cbEGF32 pair. Pathogenic in ClinVar. The one variant where a modelled answer can be checked against a measured one.
Second literature mutant (the equivalent position in cbEGF33), characterised in the same domain-context work. Not in our ClinVar set — included as a modelling control.
Pathogenic ca_EH ligand, buried (RSA 7.3%). Charge reversal next to the ion.
Pathogenic ca_D1 ligand. Removes the carboxylate outright — the maximal ligand deletion.
Pathogenic ca_EH ligand, buried (RSA 9.0%), neonatal-severe region.
Pathogenic ca_D1 ligand in the TB4-flanked construct — tests a different domain context.
Pathogenic ca_EH ligand, the most buried in the set (RSA 2.4%), X-ray reference.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the other mechanism: removes disulfide C4. Prediction — the fold is damaged but the calcium site should survive. If the ion also moves, our two mechanisms are not as separable as the manuscript claims.
NEGATIVE CONTROL: non-critical residue, AlphaMissense 0.23. Prediction — nothing moves. Bounds how much apparent ion displacement is just AF3 run-to-run noise.
